title: When the Salt Turns
premise: Zephyrine Marchetti, exiled for a storm they never meant to call, has spent seven years keeping the ledgers of the Vellum Guild, which trades in impossible things. When the border wards collapse on the night the stars go out, Zephyrine discovers the ledgers themselves were the wards' anchor — and that Guildmaster Corvane sold the kingdom's sky to the thing wearing King Aldric's crown. To restore the stars, Zephyrine must unbind the king before the last dragon-fire gutters out, choosing between loyalty to the guild that sheltered them and the truth of what it became. In the end, Zephyrine burns their own exile-name in dragon-fire to rekindle the stars, dethrones the crown-thing, and takes Corvane's place — not as master of the guild, but as its first honest ledger-keeper.
about_author: Freya Ravensworth is the pen name of a former archivist who claims to have catalogued three libraries that no longer exist. They write fantasy about paperwork, power, and the people caught between them.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A quiet night balancing the guild's strangest accounts: bottled thunder, a debt paid in years, a feather from a dragon thought extinct. Through ledger entries we learn Zephyrine's exile and their careful, rule-bound life. Emotional beat: contentment built on willful blindness, as one entry — 'one sky, sold' — slips past them unnoticed.

chapters.title: The Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The border wards fall with a sound like tearing silk; every star vanishes at once. Panic floods the guildhall as clients demand refunds on impossible things now failing. Corvane orders Zephyrine to seal the ledgers and tell no one. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into suspicion when Zephyrine realizes the wards fell from inside.

chapters.title: What the Ink Remembers
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, with an interlude from the dying dragon Emberlast. The ledgers remember everything written in them; Zephyrine finds Corvane's hidden entries recording the sale of the kingdom's sky to 'the Crown Below.' Emberlast, last keeper of dragon-fire, sends a summons carried by a moth made of ash. Emotional beat: betrayal — the guild that saved Zephyrine doomed everyone else.

chapters.title: A Debt Paid in Years
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Fleeing the guildhall, Zephyrine calls in an old guild favor from Sable Ives, a thief who once paid a debt with her own memories and remembers nothing of why she owes Zephyrine loyalty at all. Their uneasy alliance forms over a stolen map to the capital. Emotional beat: guilt — Zephyrine is using Sable exactly as Corvane used them.

chapters.title: The Road Where Maps Lie
chapters.summary: Alternating Zephyrine and Sable POVs. The starless road to the capital rearranges itself nightly, hunting travelers. Zephyrine's storm-calling, rusty and feared, is the only thing that holds the road open — forcing them to confront the exile that haunts their name. Emotional beat: reluctant self-acceptance; power is not the corruption, hiding is.

chapters.title: The Court of the Hollow King
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Infiltrating the palace as ledger-auditors, they find King Aldric lucid for ten minutes a day, trapped behind his own smiling face. He begs Zephyrine — a stranger — to check the royal accounts, knowing numbers are the one magic the crown-thing cannot rewrite. Emotional beat: horror and pity entwined; the king is a prisoner doing bookkeeping in his head.

chapters.title: Corvane's Confession
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Corvane catches Sable copying the royal ledgers and, instead of killing her, tells the truth: he sold the sky to stop a famine, believing a traded heaven was cheaper than buried children. The crown-thing has simply never stopped collecting. Emotional beat: devastating ambiguity — the villain was right, once, and then kept being wrong.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. With Aldric's own memorized figures as the key, Zephyrine begins the unbinding rite in the throne room while Sable holds off the crown-thing's courtiers, who are revealed as debts given legs. The rite requires a name freely surrendered — and Zephyrine offers their exile-name. Emotional beat: climax; sacrifice chosen not for redemption but because it is true.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon-Fire
chapters.summary: Emberlast's POV. The old dragon arrives above the capital as the crown-thing tears free of Aldric, and gives the last of its fire to reignite the stars through the wound in the sky. Aldric, freed but hollowed, abdicates into the guild's custody. Emberlast dies mid-flight, becoming a constellation. Emotional beat: grief transfigured — some prices are paid gladly.

chapters.title: First Honest Entry
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, epilogue. Stars restored, Zephyrine stands where Corvane stood, offered the guildmastership by a guild terrified of its own history. Instead they reopen the ledgers, write the truth of the last seven years in full, and hire Sable as the guild's first auditor of impossible things. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — loyalty rebuilt on truth, not silence.
